correctness.rationale: The objective is the expected uniformly seeded open-component size including the seed: conditional on a realization, multiplying by n−1 gives the sum of squared component sizes, equivalently the ordered connected-pair count. Independent exact enumeration of all labeled graphs, modulo vertex permutations, gave 1,2,6,21 connected classes. For the 28 nonexceptional classes, all 127 deletion-versus-fixed-witness comparisons were certified on the whole open interval by nonnegative coefficients after p=t/(1+t) and multiplication by (1+t)^d. There were 147 exact comparisons of the two objective constructions including repeated A/B checks. The two exceptional adjacency lists give the recorded factorizations: 4(R_A,3−R_A,1)=2p²(4p−1), and 4(R_B,2−R_B,0)=2p²(1−p)(4p−1); all strict competitor and orbit equality identities also match. Thus p=1/4 is the only interior switch and all tie sets are exactly as stated. The other classes have at least one permanent optimum, not necessarily a unique one. The endpoint exclusions are retained.
residual_risks: Exhaustive only for simple connected graphs through five vertices under the specified independent-edge preventive intervention and uniform surviving seed law. No weighted or heterogeneous model is tested.
